description: xbench vs-browsers (scripts/perf-bench/xbench.py --perf-lab run): the bench build's Chromium tab against Chrome stable as the reference arm, interleaved and rotated each round on one host from cloned template profiles, local pages only: cold launch to window and to the linked page's paint, new tab paint, tab switch, memory at 1, 10, 20 and back to 1 tab, idle CPU and wakeups at 1 and 20 tabs, and CPU energy (with billed energy and GPU time) idle in view and hidden, scrolling, playing video and switching tabs. Each row is a series per browser (xbench.<browser>.<row>); Chrome's carry its version (xbench.chrome-<version>.<row>), so a Chrome update starts new series instead of a step at a cmux commit. Each cmux row also has its per-round ratio to that Chrome (.vs-chrome-<version>), which a change of the host cancels out of. A run refuses to start when Chrome cannot be fetched.
